requirements.statement: DocForge projects open only from a directory or docforge.yaml using schema docforge.project.v1.
General documents use document.md and docforge-standard without academic metadata.
Academic metadata is a typed optional profile selected by academic templates.
Obsolete ThesisForge public contracts are absent or rejected without compatibility aliases.
Default source, build, and Review paths use neutral document filenames.
Project resources remain project-relative and reject unsafe path classes.
The deterministic semantic and DOCX pipeline preserves renderer boundaries, cancellation, and atomic output.
CLI, HTTP, Tauri, and frontend use one versioned DocForge runtime and BuildReport contract.
The installed macOS workbench and Microsoft Word preview use neutral DocForge terminology and valid outputs.
Repository examples, fixtures, documentation, packaging, CI, and release configuration use DocForge contracts.

acceptance.statement: A directory containing docforge.yaml with schema docforge.project.v1 opens through the CLI and desktop workbench.
A general project using document.md and docforge-standard completes inspect, validate, review, and build without academic metadata.
An academic project supplies a typed optional academic profile and builds without imposing those fields on general projects.
Obsolete manifest, command, aggregate, package, BuildReport, and workbench protocol identities are absent or rejected.
Default source, build, and Review paths use document.md and neutral document output names.
Project paths reject absolute, remote, traversal, and symlink-escape inputs while accepting safe relative resources.
The Markdown to ForgeDocument to RenderPlan to DOCX pipeline is deterministic, ordered, cancelable, and atomic.
CLI, HTTP, Tauri, and frontend fixtures use one versioned DocForge protocol with matching identities.
The installed macOS workbench uses neutral DocForge terminology and produces a valid Microsoft Word final preview.
Repository-owned examples, fixtures, active documentation, packaging, and CI use DocForge contracts and neutral filenames.

cases.title: Open a canonical DocForge project
cases.goal: Prove directory and manifest project entry use the strict DocForge v1 contract.
preconditions: The repository test fixtures and Python environment are available.

steps.action: Run project model, loader, and application project service tests.
steps.expected: Canonical directories and docforge.yaml open while bare Markdown and obsolete manifests are rejected.

assertions.statement: The strict DocForge project entry contract passes.

cases.title: Build a general DocForge project
cases.goal: Prove a neutral general project completes inspect, validate, review, and build without academic metadata.
preconditions: The docforge-general fixture and Python environment are available.

steps.action: Copy the general fixture to an isolated directory and run all four CLI operations.
steps.expected: All operations succeed and create neutral Review and DOCX outputs.

assertions.statement: The general project completes the neutral offline flow without academic requirements.

args: set -eu; tmp=$(mktemp -d /tmp/docforge-a2.XXXXXX); trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT; cp -R tests/fixtures/docforge-general "$tmp/project"; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m docforge.cli inspect "$tmp/project" >/dev/null; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m docforge.cli validate "$tmp/project" >/dev/null; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m docforge.cli review "$tmp/project" >/dev/null; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m docforge.cli build "$tmp/project" >/dev/null; test -s "$tmp/project/review/document.review.md"; test -s "$tmp/project/review/document.review-map.json"; test -s "$tmp/project/build/document.docx"; printf '%s\n' '{"assertion_id":"a2-general-flow","method":"equal","expected":true,"actual":true,"status":"passed"}' >> "$SPECNAV_VERIFICATION_ASSERTION_RESULT_FILE"

cases.title: Build an academic profile without global leakage
cases.goal: Prove academic fields are typed and template-scoped while general documents remain valid.
preconditions: The academic and general fixtures are available.

steps.action: Run template, compiler, project, and distribution profile tests.
steps.expected: Academic builds pass and general builds remain free of academic requirements.

assertions.statement: Academic profile requirements do not leak into general projects.

args: set -eu; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/templates tests/compiler tests/project tests/test_distribution.py -q; printf '%s\n' '{"assertion_id":"a3-profile-isolation","method":"equal","expected":true,"actual":true,"status":"passed"}' >> "$SPECNAV_VERIFICATION_ASSERTION_RESULT_FILE"

cases.title: Reject obsolete ThesisForge contracts

preconditions: Repository facticity rules and obsolete-input tests are available.

args: set -eu; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_facticity.py tests/core/test_forge_document.py tests/project -q; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python scripts/check_facticity.py --json /tmp/docforge-case-a4.json --markdown /tmp/docforge-case-a4.md; printf '%s\n' '{"assertion_id":"a4-no-obsolete-contract","method":"equal","expected":true,"actual":true,"status":"passed"}' >> "$SPECNAV_VERIFICATION_ASSERTION_RESULT_FILE"

cases.title: Preserve the deterministic DOCX pipeline
cases.goal: Prove semantic ordering, renderer boundaries, OOXML structures, cancellation, deterministic output, and atomic replacement.
preconditions: Core, compiler, renderer, application, and deterministic-output tests are available.

args: set -eu; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/core tests/compiler tests/renderers/docx tests/application tests/test_acceptance.py tests/test_compiler.py tests/test_docx_renderer.py -q; printf '%s\n' '{"assertion_id":"a7-deterministic-pipeline","method":"equal","expected":true,"actual":true,"status":"passed"}' >> "$SPECNAV_VERIFICATION_ASSERTION_RESULT_FILE"

cases.title: Keep Python, TypeScript, Rust, HTTP, and Tauri protocol parity
cases.goal: Prove all runtime boundaries use one strict versioned DocForge protocol and BuildReport identity.
preconditions: Python, frontend, and Rust dependencies are installed in the verification worktree.

steps.action: Run focused Python adapters, frontend transport tests, real HTTP acceptance, and Rust protocol tests.
steps.expected: All runtimes accept canonical identities and reject obsolete or malformed protocol data.

assertions.statement: The versioned DocForge runtime and BuildReport contract is consistent across all boundaries.

args: set -eu; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/adapters tests/application/test_build_report_contract.py tests/application/test_build_stage_lifecycle.py -q; /Users/wenliang_zeng/.nvm/versions/node/v22.19.0/bin/pnpm --dir frontend test; /Users/wenliang_zeng/.cargo/bin/cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml; printf '%s\n' '{"assertion_id":"a8-protocol-parity","method":"equal","expected":true,"actual":true,"status":"passed"}' >> "$SPECNAV_VERIFICATION_ASSERTION_RESULT_FILE"

cases.title: Verify installed DocForge and Microsoft Word preview evidence
cases.goal: Prove the installed macOS workbench uses neutral terminology and generated a valid Word PDF preview.
preconditions: The content-addressed installed acceptance receipt and screenshot are present.

steps.action: Validate the installed app receipt, Microsoft Word result, accessibility labels, and screenshot SHA-256.
steps.expected: The receipt is passed, Word preview is available, and the screenshot matches its recorded hash.

assertions.statement: Installed DocForge.app and Microsoft Word final preview evidence is internally consistent and content-addressed.

args: set -eu; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -c 'import hashlib,json,pathlib; root=pathlib.Path("openspec/changes/docforge-project-format-v1/development/tasks/006-workbench-desktop/evidence"); r=json.loads((root/"macos-native-acceptance.json").read_text()); p=root/r["evidence"]["screenshot"]; assert r["ok"] is True and r["status"]=="passed"; assert r["app"]["displayName"]=="DocForge" and r["runtime"]["manifest"]=="docforge.yaml" and r["runtime"]["source"]=="document.md"; assert r["build"]["output"]=="document.docx" and r["wordPreview"]["engine"]=="microsoft-word" and r["wordPreview"]["status"]=="available" and r["wordPreview"]["pdfGenerated"] is True; assert hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()==r["evidence"]["screenshotSha256"]; assert r["bundleVerification"]["ok"] is True; print(json.dumps({"ok":True,"word":r["wordPreview"]["microsoftWordVersion"],"screenshotSha256":r["evidence"]["screenshotSha256"]}))'; printf '%s\n' '{"assertion_id":"a9-installed-word-preview","method":"equal","expected":true,"actual":true,"status":"passed"}' >> "$SPECNAV_VERIFICATION_ASSERTION_RESULT_FILE"

args: set -eu; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python scripts/check_facticity.py --json /tmp/docforge-case-a10.json --markdown /tmp/docforge-case-a10.md; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python scripts/verify_desktop_distribution.py --platform macos --bundle-root src-tauri/target/release/bundle; PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python scripts/prepare_release.py --tag v0.1.0 --validate-only; printf '%s\n' '{"assertion_id":"a10-repository-clean","method":"equal","expected":true,"actual":true,"status":"passed"}' >> "$SPECNAV_VERIFICATION_ASSERTION_RESULT_FILE"
